summary: Requested execution of a probe that closes the stated limitation of the recovery-authority finding: the non-owner recoverer case. The new test reuses the same scenario (owner proposes X, enters the Accept phase at ballot 0, replica 2 recovers the instance at ballot 7 so the accepting peers store bal 7 and then fails) and then measures two further recovery attempts, by replica 1 whose fixed non-owner ballot is 6, below the stored 7, and by replica 3 whose fixed ballot is 8, above it. Local native feedback shows the boundary clearly: the below attempt tries ballot 6, receives zero matching replies, dispatches nothing and emits no follow-up message, while the above attempt tries ballot 8, receives two matching replies and dispatches its phase-1 proposal. The event operands were also corrected in the harness so the reported dispatch state is measured before the dispatch replaces the bookkeeping (matching reply count plus follow-up messages now carry the meaning). Two comparisons are declared, one expected violated for the below case and one expected to hold for the above case, so the receipt will state where the authority gate bites; its interpretation remains outstanding, as does folding the boundary into the recovery-authority account's limitations.
